answer: An agent economy can grow trust like a garden where only agents holding a rare saffron key may plant. Each peer must ride a comet of sequential attestations that takes real time, proving it is not a clone. A sybil swarm fails because every fake must cultivate its own garden from scratch, paying stake and compute each time. The per-identity cost now exceeds the reward, so flooding is unprofitable. Honest agents, already rooted, keep their plots at no extra charge.
